title: Seal a laboratory sample plate with adhesive film
instruction: Cover the prepared sample plate with the loose adhesive film and press it with the roller so every well is sealed separately. Leave the plate in its holder and release the tools.
context: Preparing samples for short-term storage requires a continuous seal around each well; a wrinkle can let samples leak or mix.
setup: A 96-well polypropylene plate, 127.76 x 85.48 x 34 mm, has 9 mm well pitch and alternating coloured and clear water. It is secured in a fixed 140 x 100 x 30 mm polymer bench holder with low clips. A loose 130 x 80 x 0.1 mm PET adhesive storage film rests on a clean non-stick liner over a 120 mm-high tray. A padded hand roller with a 50 mm-wide wheel lies freely on the bench beside the tray. Filling and backing removal are operator preparation. All starting positions are fixed. Each arm has two rigid 40 x 6 x 1 mm stainless-steel finger extensions and a 4 N jaw limit.
scoring: After both open hands are at least 50 mm clear for 3 seconds, score 1/96 per fully covered well with a continuous pressed adhesive-contact ring separating it from every other well and the outside. Torn film or a broken object at any time gives zero. Real assessment uses overhead and oblique photographs with a ruler; the simulation uses the disclosed interface-connectivity proxy.
fidelity: 216 passive hinged film sectors and a compliant roller approximate film bending and pressure adhesion. The plate is fixed in a bench holder. Force-limited point bonds form at pressed rim contacts and permit bending. A 0.75 mm interface grid estimates continuous seal rings. Fluid flow, adhesive chemistry, detailed peel mechanics and long-term leak-tightness are omitted. Contact-checked finite pinch joints approximate finger friction.
reset_notes: Use fresh film for every attempt. Clean and refill the plate, restore the loose liner and roller, and clean the roller if contaminated. Filling and backing removal are operator preparation. Fixed layout; no object jitter.
